A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fine-tuning Done Right in Model Editing. Their complete text, tables, figures, mathematics, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original pipeline comparisons, batch-size and tuning-location analyses, benchmark results, and experiments scaling to 100K edits and 72B models.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds MoE, medical-editing, augmentation, and larger-model baseline results in Tables 5–8.

M1.justification: The core breadth-first, mini-batch, localized fine-tuning method is unchanged. Appendix A.4 introduces the tested LocFT-BF-Aug variant, augmenting each edit prompt with five randomly prefixed texts; v1 only suggested this remedy.

E1.justification: v3 retains ZsRE, COUNTERFACT, and WikiBigEdit while adding actual evaluations on QAEdit and MedEditBench. The medical benchmark materially extends coverage beyond general factual editing into specialized medical knowledge (Appendices A.2–A.3).

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain unchanged. However, v3 adds RLEdit and UltraEdit to the larger-model scaling comparison in Table 8, where v1 Table 4 compared only LocFT-BF's location-selection strategies.

E3.justification: Existing experimental protocols are retained. Added configurations include Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B with 1000 QAEdit samples, 930 medical edits evaluated without paraphrase generalization, prefix-augmented training, and 1000-edit ZsRE baseline evaluations at 14B using default and proportional editing locations.

E4.justification: v1's suggested augmentation remedy becomes an empirical comparison with and without augmentation across three models (Table 7). v3 also tests transfer of the locating heuristic jointly to an unseen dataset and MoE architecture, and examines baseline sensitivity to location-selection strategies when scaling (Tables 5 and 8).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for its experiments. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables and plots are unchanged, but Tables 5–8 add substantial results. For example, the new augmented variant achieves COUNTERFACT generalization of 50.93/49.70/44.90 across the three models, versus 33.23/39.53/11.77 for the retained unaugmented variant. These are additional experimental results, not improved scores under unchanged training.

T1.justification: New Section 2.1 formally defines factual edits using subject–relation–object triples, the editing parameter transformation, and a sequential trajectory required to retain all previous target facts. This adds basic mathematical definitions, without introducing theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: correcting fine-tuning's pipeline and selecting tuning locations yields a leading editor that scales to 100K edits and 72B models. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 2.5 newly argues that accumulating edits, rerunning breadth-first fine-tuning, and buffering requests make sequential deployment feasible. The appendices additionally interpret heuristic transfer to MoE models and the 14B baseline results as evidence about applicability and competing methods' scalability limitations.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the MoE model's layer-20 shared-expert down-projection target and the five-prefix augmentation procedure. It removes v1's statement that source code is provided in supplementary material, without replacement access instructions; this establishes reduced disclosure, not that the code itself was withdrawn.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al.'s medical-editing benchmark work and Qwen Team's MoE model reference. The related-work discussion and positioning around correcting fine-tuning implementation remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Background and BF Pipeline for Sequential Editing subsections and expands the appendix structure. It removes the Ethics Statement, Reproducibility Statement, and LLM Usage sections and edits affiliation text, while retaining most existing prose and the main narrative sequence.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displayed evidence with dedicated MoE, medical, augmentation, and baseline-scaling tables (Tables 5–8). Existing charts are retained; introductory Figures 1 and 2 exchange numbering and placement, other floats move, and Table 4's first-column heading changes from Status to Strategy.

improvement.justification: Table 7 tests v1's previously unverified augmentation remedy, and Table 8 supplies missing larger-model baseline comparisons, improving support for retained conclusions. Medical and MoE evaluations add useful applicability evidence. These gains are bounded by the narrow additional settings and partly offset by removal of the supplementary-code access statement, yielding a modest net quality improvement.
